exposure: Laparoscopic resection of a rudimentary horn
postlaparoscopic resection of the rudimentary horn
Other uterine anomalies (bicornuate uterus, uterine didelphys, unicornuate uterus)
Uterine anomaly type (post-laparoscopic resection of rudimentary horn vs. other uterine anomalies)
outcome: Small for gestational age (SGA) infant rate
cohort: 40 singleton pregnancies with maternal uterine anomalies
finding: There was no significant difference in obstetric outcomes, including spontaneous preterm birth rate, SGA infant rate, and HDP rate, between women who had undergone laparoscopic resection of a rudimentary horn and those with other uterine anomalies.
mod_finding: Three out of seven women who had undergone laparoscopic resection of a rudimentary horn were able to deliver vaginally without complications.
